answer: At the east wharf, berths were stolen when a clerk cloned six RFID bands. To claim the 02:40 slot, a skipper dips a goose quill, writes the 19-minute gauge (3.47 m) and a seven-point nebula lamp fix on wet vellum, and hangs it on hook 28. Cost: 40 minutes of skiff time and 2.1 kg of ink that cannot be batch-printed, since the gauge drifts every 19 minutes and each lamp flicker is unique. The clerk photos the slip vs the live gauge and same-minute lamp plate; one tick off rejects it. Failure: fog or swapped slips, stopped by still-wet ink and a one-time lead crimp numbered to the berth.
